title: Add support for --output to podman build --remote
body:
<!-- Thanks for sending a pull request! -->

#### Checklist

<!-- Use [x] to mark as done, or click the checkbox after opening PR -->

This PR tries to add a feature for remote builds, currently for remote builds the streaming of rootfs is not enabled through
`--output` flag, I tired to create a API which directly streams the rootfs through tar from the server and directly to the client depending on the `type` i.e `local` or `tar`

To solve this, a new API endpoint that securely streams the built image rootfs as a tarball directly from the server to the client, without leaking temporary containers.

Also, added tests
Fixes #28342

comments.body: [NON-BLOCKING] Packit jobs failed. @podman-container-tools/packit-jobs please check. Everyone else, feel free to ignore.

I am encountering with with this `Error: exporting image rootfs: layer not known`, I am not sure why this error comes ? 

but it seems when read/write operation while mounting the image creates this error ?

The remote `--output` failures (exporting image rootfs: layer not known) come from the new server handler `ExportImageRootfs` in `pkg/api/handlers/libpod/images.go`.

It only calls `image.Mount() -> store.MountImage()`. That can return `storage.ErrLayerUnknown` ("layer not known") when the image top layer isn’t directly mountable (common with read-only image stores and in some rootless setups). Buildah already handles this in `vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/image.go`: try MountImage first, and on `ErrLayerUnknown` fall back to a short-lived container from the image, then `copier.Get()`.

Local CI passes because local `--output` still uses Buildah’s native path; remote CI fails because it hits this new `/libpod/images/{name}/rootfs` endpoint after build.

Fix: keep `image.Mount()` as the first attempt, but add the same `ErrLayerUnknown` -> temporary container mount fallback (with proper cleanup), then stream via `copier.Get()`.

> It only calls `image.Mount() -> store.MountImage()`. That can return `storage.ErrLayerUnknown` ("layer not known") when the image top layer isn’t directly mountable (common with read-only image stores and in some rootless setups). Buildah already handles this in `vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/image.go`: try MountImage first, and on `ErrLayerUnknown` fall back to a short-lived container from the image, then `copier.Get()`.
> 

So, as per my understanding the image isn't mountable because it has read only layers, creating a temporary container ensure we have a top mountable `read/write` layer on top of it but it should only be used as a fallback mechanism ? 

I know for maintaining consistency with buildah we use it as fallback mechanism
but IMO we can always create a temporary container in the first place because it always guarantees results ?

For now I have implemented it by creating a mount path using image and using a fallback if required.
